Youth-Led Protests Spread Across Europe Amid Rising Costs and Education Concerns

Massive Demonstrations Across France

For the third consecutive weekend, hundreds of thousands of protesters took to the streets across France to express frustration over the rising cost of living and the state of the education system. Government estimates suggest approximately 320,000 people participated nationwide.

While the marches were largely peaceful, authorities reported over 560 arrests as some demonstrations, particularly in Paris, ended in clashes. Police utilized tear gas and stun grenades to manage groups involved in setting fires and throwing projectiles.

Core Grievances

  • Education: Concerns regarding neglected school infrastructure and perceived unfairness in university admissions.
  • Economic Pressure: Anger regarding the rising cost of living and stagnant wages.
  • Broadening Support: While initiated by high school students, the movement has now gained support from labor unions, climate activists, and older generations.

Protests Across Europe

The wave of youth-led unrest extended to other European nations, with organizers citing demands for improved social services, climate protection, and affordable housing.

  • Germany: The "Gen Z regelt" initiative held rallies in over 30 cities. While many were peaceful, violence erupted in cities like Frankfurt, Cologne, and Hamburg, involving storefront damage and confrontations with police.
  • Portugal: Thousands marched in Lisbon, focusing specifically on the national housing crisis.
  • Netherlands: Increased police presence was noted in The Hague following online calls for protests, though no major disturbances were reported.

Official Response

French authorities deployed roughly 70,000 police and gendarmes, citing a "very high risk" of disorder. Protests in Paris were rerouted away from city centers to protect commercial and government areas, and temporary curfews were implemented in specific zones. To verify specific attendance figures or further government updates, readers should consult official press releases from the respective interior ministries or monitor local verified news reports.
